about: Generalisation design G23 (train), in dev.json format. Tier 4 = a real product: a bought-in camera module placed from the parts catalogue into a pocket, a lens window and field of view kept clear, a ribbon-cable slot sized from the cable, a captive hex nut for a tripod stud, and fit / retention / installation checks against reference models and keep-out volumes. One printed body. L1 ids match requirements.md next to this file, which holds the L2/L3 tree, reference models, assumptions and traceability. Numbers that are not in the request words (clearance bands, lip overlap, ribbon width) come from requirements.md and are provisional until the owner confirms them. Never put any of these numbers in agent logic: they belong in the request text and in generalize/parts/*/part.json.

methods.inspection: read from the design or mesh (counts, sizes, positions, relations)
methods.analysis: computed by Python (connectivity, interference and clearance against reference models, swept motion, hand calculations)
methods.demonstration: a stand-in object is placed in the design (fits, rests, does not slide)
methods.test: a probe is applied (insert the camera along a straight path, insert the nut, pass the ribbon)

requests.title: RPi camera pocket mount with 1/4-20 base
requests.request: A holder for a Raspberry Pi camera v2 board: 25 x 24 mm, 9 mm tall including the lens, with four 2.2 mm holes on a 21 x 12.5 mm pattern and a ribbon connector on the back. The board sits in a pocket and is held without screws by lips that reach 0.6 to 1.15 mm over its front face. The 8 mm lens looks out through a window that is clear of any wall (no wall within 0.5 mm of the lens barrel, and nothing in the camera's 62 x 49 degree field of view; the board's orientation to the sensor axes is not known, so use the 62 degree angle on both axes). The 16 mm wide ribbon cable leaves through the back of the holder through a slot 17 mm wide and no more than 10 mm long. The base of the holder has a hex pocket for a 1/4-20 nut (11.1 mm across flats, 5.6 mm thick, held in a hex pocket 0.1 to 0.3 mm bigger than the nut on each flat, with a stud hole 6.4 to 6.8 mm in diameter and a seat 2.0 to 3.65 mm thick) so it screws onto a tripod stud 10 mm long. Print it in one piece on an FDM printer without supports, in the orientation you state. It is no larger than 45 x 45 x 30 mm.
requests.request_verbatim: A holder for a Raspberry Pi camera v2 (25 x 24 x 9 mm, holes 21 x 12.5 mm) with the lens window clear of any wall at 8 mm diameter. The base has a 1/4-20 hex nut pocket so I can put it on a tripod. The ribbon cable exits the back through a 17 mm wide slot.
requests.request_notes: Added to the owner's words, all from requirements.md section 3 or the catalogue datasheets: 'held without screws' (A8); ribbon width 16 mm (A5); field of view 62.2 x 48.8 degrees (catalogue); nut size and stud length 10 mm (A6, A7); 'no wall within 0.5 mm of the lens barrel' is the reading of 'clear of any wall at 8 mm' (A3); FDM, one piece, no supports (A9); size limit 45 x 45 x 30 (A10). Audit additions from requirements.md: lip overlap band (L2.3.2), both-axes field of view (A4), slot length 10 (L2.5.3), nut pocket and seat bands (A6, A7).

l1.text: The design shall place the camera board from the parts catalogue in the holder, with its lens looking out of the front, and shall declare that layout, the direction the board is installed from and the tripod stud axis.

The 25 x 24 mm board shall sit in a pocket with 0.15 to 0.35 mm clearance on each edge, resting on printed supports under its edges and clear of its ribbon connector, lens and every other printed surface.

The board shall be held in the pocket without screws: it shall move at most 0.8 mm sideways and 1.0 mm out of the pocket, with at least two retaining lips on opposite sides over its front face, each reaching 0.6 to 1.15 mm over the board.

The 8 mm lens window shall be clear: no printed surface within 0.5 mm of the lens barrel, and nothing inside the lens's keep-out cylinder or its field of view (the 62 degree angle taken on both axes, the sensor orientation being unknown).

The 16 mm wide ribbon cable shall leave through the back of the holder through a slot 17 mm wide and at most 10 mm long, with its straight path of 20 mm behind the connector clear of the holder by at least 0.4 mm.

The base shall hold a 1/4-20 hex nut (11.1 mm across flats, 5.6 mm thick) in a hex pocket that stops it turning (0.1 to 0.3 mm over the nut on each flat), with a 6.4 to 6.8 mm stud hole, a seat 2.0 to 3.65 mm thick and room for a 10 mm stud to pass through the nut, so the holder screws onto a tripod.
The tripod stud axis shall be perpendicular to the lens axis and centred across the board, entering a flat base face at least 20 mm across.

The board shall install into the pocket by one straight movement from outside, and the hex nut shall go into its pocket by one straight movement, each without touching the holder on the way (the retaining lips may flex).
The holder shall be one manifold body that prints on an FDM printer without supports in its stated orientation, with walls 2 to 4 mm thick.
The holder shall be no larger than 45 x 45 x 30 mm.
The design shall be delivered as an STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout and the agent's own clearance report, and that report shall agree with an independent measurement.

beyond_library: subtraction: a pocket for a board, a stepped lens window, a ribbon slot, a hex nut pocket with a stud hole
parts catalogue: load part.json models (camera board, tripod stud) and place them by datums
retention without fasteners: edge supports, lips over the board's front face, travel limits derived from the board's size
envelope generation: lens keep-out, field-of-view pyramid, ribbon path, stud, nut and install sweeps
a hex pocket sized from across-flats with a per-flat clearance and a print orientation that needs no support
interference checks against external solids: clear_of, travel, aperture width, swept installation
